name: Grindelia

project_scope.selection_mode: B062 baseline + 2026-10-12 Genus Comparison Builder four-canonical-species expansion
source_pool_concept_notes: Grindelia papposa is treated as an alias of canonical G. ciliata; not an additional card.
Grindelia nuda var. nuda belongs with the canonical G. nuda concept; do not double-count.
Grindelia squarrosa remains source-pool comparison-only in this module; do not silently install it or map it to G. nuda without name-level evidence.
project_scope.canonical_installation: All four focal accepted concepts are already in data/manifest.json; this change does not install species.
project_scope.hold_interpretation: Legacy B062 holds refer to scientific/range review at the time, not missing canonical installation. Canonical manifest now includes adenodonta and ciliata; squarrosa is not installed. Preserve range metadata in each species card.

study_strategy.warning: Historical Grindelia names in Central Texas overlap heavily. Always reconcile old var./synonym names before counting counties.

quick_split: G. nuda — rayless curlytop gumweed; gland-dotted aromatic foliage; PASS.
G. adenodonta — radiate, hairy/glandular-stemmed, hooked/recurved phyllaries; range HOLD.
G. squarrosa — radiate, squarrose/recurved phyllaries; current-concept range HOLD.
G. ciliata — accepted name for old G. papposa; annual, radiate, many-bristled pappus; range HOLD.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Look at the sticky flower-head involucre from the SIDE, then examine one mature cypsela and its pappus. The combination of many resin-tipped phyllaries around a composite head, alternate usually toothed leaves, and distinctive pappus is much stronger than yellow color.
shared_traits: Asteraceae composite heads with numerous tubular disk florets; rays may be present or absent, so raylessness alone does not exclude Grindelia.
Multiple rows of persistent narrow involucral phyllaries; tips often resinous, spreading, hooked, recurved, or nearly straight depending on species and phyllary position.
Alternate mostly simple leaves, upper leaves commonly sessile to clasping; teeth may be pointed or resin-tipped; resin glands occur on heads and often foliage.
Cypselae (one-seeded dry fruits) carry a pappus; its count, shape, persistence and length are key reproductive characters.

terminology.point_to: Individual narrow bract below the entire head, not a petal or a sepal.
Peripheral strap-shaped floret, present in three focal species and absent in typical G. nuda.
Small tubular floret in the center of the head.
Mature one-seeded fruit; examine detached naturally mature fruit, not an immature ovary.
Awns, bristles or scales arising at the top of the cypsela; count with magnification.
Tiny resin dots versus projecting multicellular hairs on stem and leaf surfaces; use a hand lens.

look_here_first_sequence.look: Mature head FACE and SIDE, same individual
look_here_first_sequence.action: Check for rays; rayless + dense gland dots suggests canonical G. nuda, but confirm with head and leaves.

look_here_first_sequence.look: Mature cypsela with pappus under 10–20× magnification
look_here_first_sequence.action: Many barbellate bristles (25–40) plus longer awns/scales strongly support G. ciliata; only about two awns points toward other species and requires follow-up.

look_here_first_sequence.look: Upper flowering stem and both faces of mid-stem leaves
look_here_first_sequence.action: Dense short hairs and pitted glands on broad ovate/triangular leaves favor G. adenodonta; nearly glabrous leaves and stems suggest G. ciliata or G. lanceolata.

look_here_first_sequence.look: One mature mid-stem leaf against a ruler
look_here_first_sequence.action: For G. lanceolata, leaf length commonly 3–12 times width, with pointed teeth; G. ciliata commonly 2–4 times width, with oblong/obovate blades. Overlap means use fruit and head too.

look_here_first_sequence.look: Phyllaries from side at equal magnification
look_here_first_sequence.action: G. adenodonta often has hooked/recurved tips; FNA G. lanceolata usually has slightly recurved to straight/incurved tips, not strongly reflexed. Phyllary posture alone is not decisive.

look_here_first_sequence.look: Specimen without mature fruit or contradictory characters
look_here_first_sequence.action: Leave at Grindelia sp. or a tentative pair; preserve a targeted review handoff rather than force an ID.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Typically rayless/discoid in existing canonical concept
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Strong first split for nuda; count rays on intact open heads; not enough to separate radiate taxa.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia adenodonta: Usually 2 straight to weakly contorted smooth bristles/awns, 5–6 mm, tips often dilated
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia ciliata: 25–40 barbellate bristles 3–7+ mm subtending 8–15+ longer awns/scales 7–10 mm
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia lanceolata: 2 straight smooth awns, 4–8 mm, often dilated apically
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Exact count/length not yet independently reconciled against current canonical nuda concept
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Most powerful separator for ciliata; maturity and loss of readily falling awns are cautions.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia adenodonta: Distally short-hairy to somewhat villous, sometimes less hairy at base
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia lanceolata: Usually glabrous, rarely sparsely pilose near base
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Glabrous or nearly so, conspicuously gland-dotted in canonical lesson
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Photograph hairs and glands separately; sticky resin is not equivalent to hairs.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia adenodonta: Ovate/triangular to oblong or obovate, length ~1.5–3(–4+) × width
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia ciliata: Oblong to obovate, length usually 2–4 × width
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Variable oval to narrower serrate sessile/clasping leaves; not reliable alone
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Measure mature mid-stem blades; overlap especially adenodonta/ciliata.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: No project-verified numeric range for this accepted concept
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: These overlap substantially; do not build a length-only key.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Serrate and gland-dotted in current project concept
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Use close-up with 10-mm scale; count along comparable mature mid-stem margin.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia adenodonta: Hooked to recurved or nearly straight; moderately resinous
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia ciliata: Recurved to straight; slightly to moderately resinous
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia lanceolata: Usually slightly recurved, straight or incurved; weakly spreading to appressed
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Narrow spreading/ascending resin-tipped phyllaries in canonical description
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Outer and inner series differ; record position; strongly recurved is NOT a secure lanceolata diagnostic.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Biennial/short-lived subshrub in existing canonical lesson
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Support only; requires base/season context and overlaps among taxa.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia ciliata: Single or open to crowded corymbiform arrays
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Usually solitary terminal heads in existing canonical description
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Weak tie-breaker; not sufficient by itself.
Dimensions overlap; show exactly where measured excluding phyllary tips.

species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia adenodonta: 3–4.5 mm; outer often rugose, inner striate
species_comparison_matrix.Grindelia nuda: Existing canonical describes rayless head but lacks measured fruit key
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Compare fully ripe cypselae from same head, especially outer vs inner fruit.

overlap_cautions: Do not identify radiate Grindelia from yellow rays or sticky heads alone; three canonical focal species are radiate and share resinous phyllaries.
G. ciliata has a very distinctive many-bristled pappus; check a fully mature fruit and distinguish a readily lost pappus from one genuinely absent.

FNA describes G. lanceolata phyllary apices as slightly recurved, straight or incurved. The existing species card says strongly recurved or spreading; flag this conflict for species-level correction, not a genus-level assertion.
G. adenodonta and G. ciliata may have overlapping leaf lengths and ray counts; use stem hairs, mature pappus and leaf teeth together.

Historical G. papposa maps to current canonical G. ciliata. G. nuda var. nuda is represented by current canonical G. nuda. G. squarrosa must remain a separate source-pool comparison concept unless explicitly reconciled.

Flora of North America's older broad treatment/key does not independently key the project's accepted G. nuda concept as a separate terminal in the same way; keep the settled canonical mapping and request targeted concept-level character verification rather than reopening range.
Leaf tooth form and phyllary posture can vary within a head and plant; photograph outer and inner phyllary series and multiple mature leaves.
Photo checklist is a plan only; existing species photographs are not automatically proof that every diagnostic macro is covered.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.name: Grindelia squarrosa
local_source_pool_lookalikes.role: same-genus source-pool comparison, not canonical species in current manifest
local_source_pool_lookalikes.distinguish: Often looped/hooked squarrose phyllary tips; can mimic adenodonta. Check stem hairs, leaf-tooth type and mature pappus; do not conflate with old G. squarrosa var. nuda names.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.name: Heterotheca subaxillaris / H. villosa
local_source_pool_lookalikes.distinguish: Heads may have yellow rays but lack the same strongly gummy, multiseriate Grindelia involucre; inspect phyllaries and fruit pappus rather than color.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.name: Chrysopsis texana
local_source_pool_lookalikes.distinguish: Yellow-rayed composite; examine pubescence and head bracts/pappus, not ray color, before applying a gumweed name.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.name: Helianthus annuus / H. maximiliani
local_source_pool_lookalikes.distinguish: Typically broader, flatter phyllaries and distinct sunflower heads; compare receptacle, leaves and fruit rather than yellow rays.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched full-open head face; count peripheral strap-shaped ray florets, label disk vs rays; include mm scale.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Rayless nuda versus radiate others; photo of bud alone does not prove absence of rays.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: Head side: phyllary series and tip curvature
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Macro side view of entire involucre, one outer and one inner phyllary in focus; arrows for resin tip, angle and series position.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Show adenodonta hooked tips vs lanceolata usually slightly recurved/straight, but note variability.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: 10–20× macro/dissecting scope with 1-mm grid; count bristles and awns and measure lengths; include fruit from intact ripe head.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Ciliata many bristles versus usually 2 awns in adenodonta/lanceolata.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Same-magnification upper flowering stem and leaf surface; side lighting for projecting hairs, separate arrow for resin dots.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Adenodonta distal hairiness vs glabrous ciliata/lanceolata; nuda gland-dotted.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Fully expanded mid-stem leaf in situ with ruler, attachment node and both faces; trace blade length/width and clasping base.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Separate narrow lanceolata from broader forms as supporting character; demonstrate overlap.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched 10-mm margin macros, count teeth per cm and show rounded resin-tipped vs sharply pointed teeth.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Support adenodonta versus ciliata/lanceolata; annotate margin section.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: Whole flowering plant and head arrangement
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched habit shot showing base, stem branches and complete terminal array; plant height scale where possible.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Support annual/biennial/perennial and solitary vs array without overstating.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Side-by-side outer and inner mature cypselae with scale; focus on rugose/striate faces and coronate/knobby apex.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Especially adenodonta fruit variation; do not use immature ovaries.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Licensed exact-concept mature cypsela and pappus macro plus voucher identity, for comparison with FNA-style Grindelia key.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Targeted scientific verification before numeric nuda fruit/pappus assertions.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.taxa: Grindelia squarrosa and Heterotheca spp. if verified
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Same-scale involucre sides, leaf margin and fruit macros; source pool IDs and licensing required.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.why: Avoid mislabeling a squarrosa/nuda synonym concept or generic yellow daisy.

existing_media_reuse.note: Counts read from existing species.json images[] on 2026-10-12. Not newly acquired or diagnostic-photo verified. Reuse exact licensed assets and project/Joey frames only after confirming character visibility and provenance.

handoffs.issue: Canonical card currently says phyllaries strongly recurved/spreading, but FNA describes apices slightly recurved/straight/incurved. Review specimen concept and correct species card if supported; do not alter settled range.
Verify mature cypsela/pappus characters against current accepted concept and reconcile FNA older key naming without changing canonical synonym/range decisions by assumption.

Prioritize P3 many-bristled ciliata pappus, P4 adenodonta stem hairs, P2 lanceolata phyllary tip, and P1 rayless nuda. Use existing licensed exact-species media first; arrows on true diagnostic structures.
All four focal species already canonical in data/manifest.json; no installation requested. G. squarrosa source-pool entry is comparison-only here pending separate identity/review workflow.
